transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-14
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Aisha Patel (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Jordan Kim (Redwood Product), Sofia Ramirez (Nebula Head of ML), Evan Brooks (Nebula Platform), Priya Nair (Nebula Security)

Summary (auto): Quick console walkthrough focused on tracing, error analysis, request logs and end-to-end debugging flows. Customer interested in POC for production-like error scenarios and verifying SOC2/KMS controls.

Topics: tracing overview, request-log export, deduping and KV cache, error classification, private deployment considerations, SSO/SAML, audit logs, POC next steps.

Transcript:
[00:00] Aisha: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, happy Valentines, uh, I mean happy Monday, um — I'm Aisha, AE at Redwood — I'll run intro, Marcus will do the console walkthrough and Jordan will chime on product questions.
[00:18] Sofia: Hey thanks, excited — we've been looking at your tracing thing, Evan and Priya are on for infra and security questions.
[00:25] Marcus: Cool, quick agenda: we'll show tracing UI, how we map requests to spans, error buckets, and then a flow for pulling request logs and doing a root-cause debug. We'll also highlight what you can do in Dedicated/VPC if you need isolation.
[00:40] Evan: Good. We're particularly interested in debugging downstream latency spikes and intermittent 5xxs when peak traffic hits.
[00:48] Marcus: Yep, makes sense. I'll start screen share — bear with me while the demo environment loads.
[01:12] Marcus: Alright, this is the Console home — go to Tracing -> Request traces. We group by trace id, we capture metadata: model, route, tenant id, seq len, tokens, and then you can click into a trace to see the tokens and KV cache hits.
[01:35] Marcus: Note: the auto captions here may say KV cache as 'kayv cash' sometimes in logs, transcription is a bit noisy.
[01:47] Sofia: ha, noted. Can you filter by model version and by quantization profile?
[01:52] Marcus: Yes — filter at top. You can also route by model variant in the trace details, and when a fallback happened we show which variant served the request.
[02:10] Jordan: We also surface a confidence estimate that tries to detect hallucinations — it's experimental but helpful for triage.
[02:20] Priya: Where is the audit info — like who reconfigured the route or rollback history? That's big for us.
[02:26] Marcus: Under Audit & Logs — we keep change history, user IDs, and we log config rollbacks. For Private deployments we can integrate with your KMS and SIEM.
[02:40] Evan: What's retention on request logs by default?
[02:44] Aisha: Hosted default is 30 days, we have add-on for extended retention; for Dedicated you can set retention policies with the contract.
[02:54] Priya: And encryption at rest? KMS?
[02:57] Aisha: Yes, customer-managed KMS is available for Private and Dedicated, hosted uses Redwood-managed KMS but we support bring-your-own-key for Dedicated.
[03:12] Marcus: Back to traces — here's a trace with elevated latency. You can see per-step timings: model queuing, kernel execution, kv cache hit ratio.
[03:30] Marcus: In this trace you can see a big spike in 'model queuing' — when batching saturated the pool, we fall back to a gr youp (group) of smaller batches, you can see the fallback policy fired.
[03:48] Evan: Is that controllable? We want to prioritize low-latency traffic for certain routes.
[03:53] Marcus: Yes — routing policies allow priority tags, dedicated pools, and hard SLO pinning. You can promote routes to higher priority or pin to Dedicated.
[04:10] Sofia: Can we replay a trace with the same tokens to reproduce the issue?
[04:15] Marcus: Yep — export trace, or use the "Replay" action to re-run against a pinned variant. Replay preserves model version, prompt, and KV cache snapshot if available — small caveat: stochastic sampling differences may occur unless you set seed.
[04:38] Priya: About logs, do you support raw request exports? We need them for internal compliance and ingestion into Splunk.
[04:44] Marcus: We do — Request Logs -> Export. You can select date range, tenant, and choose parity of PII redaction. For Splunk we provide a CSV/JSON webhook.
[05:02] Evan: What's the typical size of a day's request log for our expected volume? (Sofia pipes in: "around 2M tokens/day")
[05:10] Marcus: For 2M tokens/day, raw logs with token-level detail can be big — roughly 1.5–2 GB depending on captured fields; we usually recommend sampling or token-aggregation for long-term storage.
[05:28] Sofia: Do you do prefix/KV cache dedupe in logs or is that separate?
[05:32] Marcus: The console flags cache hits per request — logs include a cache_hit boolean and cache_key if enabled. Deduping is part of the Optimize tool but we annotate traces for quick analysis.
[05:46] Aisha: Quick interjection — Marcus, can you demo the error analysis view?
[05:50] Marcus: Sure — Error Analysis tab aggregates errors by class: timeouts, model runtime exceptions, decode errors, and policy blocks. Clicking a class shows top offending prompts and sample traces.
[06:10] Marcus: Here's a cluster of timeouts — drill in and you get the stack: network egress, upstream model node OOM, or request queuing. We surface probable causes and often link to the route config that caused low burst capacity.
[06:30] Evan: For OOMs, do you show footprint information so we can tune batch sizes and quant profiles?
[06:35] Marcus: We expose memory footprint estimates per model variant and per sequence length. The Optimize tab will recommend quantization and batch windows.
[06:46] Sofia: Nice. About privacy: are tokens stored plaintext? Can we redact prompts?
[06:51] Aisha: We support token redaction and field-level PII redaction on export. Hosted stores tokens encrypted at rest; Private lets you control retention and encryption keys.
[07:05] Priya: Are there any known issues with request logs truncating long prompts? We have some prompts that are 6k tokens.
[07:13] Marcus: The console truncates at a configurable limit — default 4k tokens in hosted to manage storage. For Dedicated/Private we can bump limits per your contract.
[07:28] Evan: Can we instrument our own tracing spans? Like add application-level spans that show our pre-processing and post-processing times?
[07:34] Marcus: Yes — the SDK supports user spans and custom attributes. You can inject correlating ids and they'll appear in the trace timeline.
[07:45] Sofia: Excellent. Can we create alerts off trace anomalies? E.g., if error rate > 1% for a route.
[07:51] Jordan: Alerts exist — you can create per-route anomaly detection and tie to Slack/webhook. We also have automatic regression alerts from Redwood Optimize when quality drops.
[08:05] Priya: One more security question: SSO and RBAC integration — do you support SCIM and role sync?
[08:10] Aisha: Yes, SAML/SSO + SCIM user provisioning and fine-grained RBAC are supported for Enterprise.
[08:18] Marcus: Back to the demo — I'm going to show a request logs export flow now. I'll filter by tenant = nebula-prod, date range last 24 hours, and select include token timestamps.
[08:40] Marcus: Exporting — takes a few seconds — here's a sample JSON row. Note transcription may mangle a column name like 'response_time_ms' to 'response time'.
[08:55] Marcus: Sample row: {trace_id: "t-1234", route: "/inference/summary", model: "rw-m-distil-v1", tokens: 412, cache_hit: false, latency_ms: 842, error_class: null} — again names are slightly reworded in the UI on the demo env.
[09:15] Evan: For POC we'll want a raw export with all token-level details and timestamps so we can reproduce exactly, is that doable?
[09:22] Marcus: Yes, for POC we'll enable detailed logging for a limited window; we'll also show how to sample and anonymize.
[09:30] Sofia: What about scaling the POC? If we run synthetic load, can you give us a dedicated pool for the test window?
[09:36] Aisha: We can provide a small Dedicated pool for POC or use reserved capacity in our sandbox. We should size it based on tokens/sec; Marcus will advise.
[09:46] Marcus: Quick note — when you run synthetic load, watch for KV cache warmup effects. Early traffic will hit cache miss and appear slower; subsequent runs will show improved latency.
[09:58] Evan: Noted.
[10:02] Marcus: I'm now showing the replay flow — you can take a trace and open the replay modal, set a seed and target variant, and replay. There is also a "dry-run" that won't count against quotas for testing.
[10:18] Sofia: Good. Does replay preserve headers and metadata for end-to-end reproduction?
[10:22] Marcus: Yep, you can include headers, user attributes, and we can mirror the same routing policy.
[10:30] Priya: For compliance, we need an immutable audit of all replays. Is that logged?
[10:35] Jordan: Replays generate an audit entry with replay id, who triggered it, and the original trace id. You can export audit logs via the Audit API.
[10:46] Aisha: Switching gears — small talk: how's adoption looking? (laughter)
[10:54] Marcus: Back to error analysis — here's a decode error cluster we saw on one route; clicking in shows the offending prompt and candidate tokens that caused the exception. We give recommended remediations like smaller context window or fallback to smaller variant.
[11:12] Evan: Do you show model-side logs (runtime stack traces) or only the orchestration layer?
[11:18] Marcus: We try to correlate model node logs — for Private deployments customers can ship us the runtime logs or we can ingest them into the trace. In hosted we surface summarized runtime errors and attach sample stack where possible.
[11:35] Sofia: How do we get the raw log for an OOM event? We need it for root cause with our infra team.
[11:41] Marcus: We'll export the trace with linked runtime artifact; for POC we'll enable model runtime debug mode for a short window. We'll include instructions in the benchmark doc.
[12:00] Priya: Are there SLA guarantees around debug artifacts retention?
[12:06] Aisha: Retention of debug artifacts is configurable in Dedicated contracts; hosted debug artifacts are subject to the retention tier, but we can provide extended retention as an add-on.
[12:20] Evan: One operational question — if we need a hotfix rollback, does console give a one-click rollback of route config?
[12:26] Marcus: Yes — rollout history and rollback are in the Rollouts page; canary and A/B are supported and you can trigger instant rollback — rollback events are recorded for audit.
[12:40] Sofia: Can you demonstrate a failure scenario end-to-end?
[12:44] Marcus: Sure — I'll induce a simulated queue spike on the demo route.
[12:58] Marcus: You can see the queue length climb, the trace shows increased queuing time, and error rate ticks up. Error analysis ties it to a misconfigured autoscaler threshold on the route.
[13:20] Sofia: In a real environment we'd expect similar signs — nice that it surfaces the route config.
[13:28] Aisha: Quick clarification — for KV cache eviction policies, do you support TTL and LRU?
[13:33] Marcus: TTL and size-based eviction; LRU semantics are approximate for performance.
[13:42] Priya: Any notes on data residency — we are EU-only for production.
[13:47] Aisha: We have EU regions and can pin processing to region; for Private we can deploy in your VPC in eu-west.
[13:58] Evan: Cool.
[14:02] Marcus: Wrapping up demo — we covered trace drilling, playback, request-log export, error analysis, replay, and audit.
[14:10] Sofia: A few questions from our side: 1) We'll need SOC2 + network diagram, 2) Baseline runway for POC costs, 3) Steps to enable detailed logging for a limited window.
[14:22] Aisha: We'll send security docs and a benchmark workbook. Marcus will lead the logging enable steps.
[14:30] Marcus: I'll add a short step-by-step in the workbook and a sample script to export traces and request logs.
[14:38] Priya: For POC acceptance criteria: we want to see consistent latency under 300ms P50 for our critical route, error rate below 0.5%, and reproducible debug artifacts.
[14:52] Aisha: Great — we'll capture those as POC success criteria in the follow up.
[15:00] Evan: Any blockers on compliance for us to start?
[15:05] Priya: We'll need to review SOC2 and confirm KMS approach, but no legal blockers yet.
[15:12] Aisha: Ok, next steps recap: I'll send security pack and propose POC times; Marcus will share benchmark workbook and logging how-to; Evan will provide sample traffic and failure cases.
[15:28] Sofia: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[15:32] Aisha: Thanks all, we'll follow up by Wednesday. Bye.

Auto-generated action items (end of transcript): 1) Send SOC2 + network diagram (Aisha) 2) Share benchmark workbook & export guide (Marcus) 3) Customer to provide sample traffic + failure scenarios (Evan).

Notes on transcription quality: Medium — occasional word swaps and punctuation issues, proper nouns sometimes mangled.
